correctness.rationale: Derived size-biased star binomial tail and size-biased path run formula from edge independence. Conditional coefficients in the degree-(n-1) Bernstein basis have one positive-to-negative sign switch: the ratio H_j is strictly log-concave and the final nonzero coefficient has sign t(t-1)-(n-1). Division by the first negative Bernstein term makes the normalized difference strictly decreasing, proving unique transverse crossing when n>=t(t-1)+2. Endpoint n=3 is isomorphic, t=2 is strictly lower for the star and t=n equal. Ordered-pair tree distances prove larger star expectation. Independent exact enumeration covers n=3..8 and p=1/3,2/3; signs and endpoint coefficient checked to n=49 and the n=8,t=3 root polynomial factored symbolically. Finite tests corroborate, do not prove, all n.

originality.rationale: The exact random-root percolation object appears in Jevtic–Lanchier–La Salle 2020, but its available abstract describes first and second moments; their whole paper was not accessible. Newman–Jensen–Ziff use generating functions on a different small-world geometry, and Kenah–Robins distinguish independent edge percolation from correlated SIR. The audited theorem adds a sharp finite star/path tail-risk single-crossover law that is not an implication of those inspected moment or model-general statements. Potential uninspected exact distributions and extremal-tree reliability predecessors remain a material priority risk.

value.rationale: The distinction between mean outbreak magnitude and tail-exceedance risk in the simplest two finite epidemic topologies is substantively motivated. A sharp population-vs-threshold boundary, a unique transverse transmissibility crossing, and the minimal eight-vertex case constitute an interpretable infinite-family structural phase diagram, not a routine change of variables. Relevant under explicitly independent homogeneous edge transmission, not general SIR infectious periods.

final_claim: For a uniformly seeded independent-bond-percolation cluster on S_n or P_n, the star has larger mean, but for 3 <= t < n there is precisely one star/path tail-risk crossing if and only if n >= t(t-1)+2; otherwise the star tail dominates. At t=2 the star tail is smaller, and at t=n the tails are equal.
